composition_parti.rule: Regular ganged openings at 8 to 14 ft centres on the principal elevation, with the garage terminating one end; heads generally aligned within a storey.
composition_parti.note: Fixes a cascade bug: the resolved kit previously inherited 'strict-bilateral-odd-bay' (eclectic-revivals + colonial-revival, via the family splice), overstating this node's own near-symmetrical, plan-driven composition as a strict classical one.

variants.note: 'Simple dominant gable forms with minimal cross-gabling and a legible single roof hierarchy' (defining_characteristics).
Overrides the cascade's inherited value (shingle-style, via colonial-revival's family). Not named anywhere in this node's own text; the roof is one clear gable, not a broken multi-plane form.

roof_form.rule: Simple dominant gable forms with minimal cross-gabling and a legible single roof hierarchy -- the opposite of the neo-eclectic gable proliferation this node reacts against.

pitch_as_built_typical_range.note: The market-built figure, below the style's own vernacular source of 10:12-12:12 -- recorded diagnostically.

roof_pitch.rule: Principal gable pitch not less than 6:12, and 10:12 preferred; below 8:12 the mass reads as a shed and the quoted vernacular silhouette is lost (hard constraint c01).
roof_pitch.note: Direct quote of constraint c01. Fixes a cascade bug: the resolved kit previously inherited 'pitch_min=9:12' from queen-anne-american (via the family splice) as though it were this node's own hard floor, when in fact 9:12 sits well inside this node's own preferred range and above its actual hard floor of 6:12 -- overstating the requirement while citing the wrong source entirely.

variants.note: 'At porches, dormers, or the whole roof' (defining_characteristics).
Overrides the cascade's inherited value (mediterranean-vernacular, via the family splice). Nothing in this node's text or lineage supports a Mediterranean clay tile roof.

roof_material.rule: Standing-seam metal roofing at porches, dormers, or the whole roof -- one of the style's own named defining characteristics.

as_built_overhang_range_in.note: The market-built figure, below the style's own hard floor -- recorded diagnostically.

eave_condition.rule: Rake overhang not less than 8 in and eave overhang not less than 12 in, with a returned or moulded termination at every gable corner; zero-overhang boxed rakes are forbidden (hard constraint c02).
eave_condition.note: Direct quote of constraint c02. Fixes a cascade bug: the resolved kit previously inherited shingle-style's 12 in ceiling (via the family splice) as a maximum, when this node's own text states 12 in as a floor -- the opposite direction, and the exact deviation the node's own long description names as one of its five measurable failures.

height_proportion.rule: Ground plate 9 to 10 ft, with window head at 8 ft 0 in -- the open great-room plan's own driver of the head-to-soffit gap that constraint c03 exists to close.
height_proportion.note: Direct quote of typical_ratios and defining_characteristics item 6.

wing_strategy.rule: Grows by an ell rather than a stacked gable -- 'the ell gives a secondary mass without requiring a stacked gable' (massing_affinities), the massing the idiom handles best.
wing_strategy.note: Direct quote of massing_affinities note on linear-ell-farmhouse (canonical).

variants.note: Overrides the cascade's inherited value (shingle-style, via colonial-revival's family). No source names shingle cladding for this node.

primary_cladding.rule: Vertical board-and-batten or narrow lap siding, or the two combined by storey, in a single light value. Battens at 16 or 24 in on centre aligned to the framing, minimum 1x2 nominal with not less than 3/4 in projection; battens at 12 in centres or under 1/2 in projection read as stripes rather than boarding (soft constraint c04).
primary_cladding.note: Direct quote of defining_characteristics item 2 and constraint c04.

color_strategy.rule: High-contrast dark window frames, trim, and roof accents against a light wall -- a strict two-value palette, with wall-to-trim luminance contrast greater than 8:1, doing the work of profile depth that shallow overhangs and boxed rakes no longer do.
color_strategy.note: Direct quote of defining_characteristics item 3 and typical_ratios. Fixes a cascade bug: the resolved kit previously inherited gothic-revival-american's 'landscape-tone-body' rule (via the family splice) forbidding white body colour -- the literal opposite of this style's white-wall, black-trim signature.

window_grouping_rule.rule_append: Window heads shall sit not more than 10 in below the soffit or frieze line. Where the plate exceeds 9 ft, either raise the head or introduce a transom to close the gap (hard constraint c03) -- a genuine advance over neo-eclectic's unaligned heads, and a sharper rule than the family's shared single-datum principle alone states.
window_grouping_rule.note: Extends the family's already-correct single-datum binding with this node's own additional numeric ceiling on head-to-soffit distance, which the node's own text names as one of its five measurable failure dimensions when violated (typical_ratios: 'as built 12 to 24 in; vernacular source 6 to 10 in').

variants.note: A real classical-depth element this node's own ornament-absent aesthetic does not carry.

entry_door.rule: 'Ornament essentially absent: no shutters, no keystones, no applied classical elements' (defining_characteristics item 7) rules out a raised-and-fielded panel door as much as it rules out a classical surround; no positive door type is named in the node's own text.
entry_door.note: Fixes a cascade bug: the previously-resolved value (georgian-colonial-american, via the family splice) is Georgian Colonial's own high-style door and contradicts defining_characteristics item 7 directly. Only the forbidding is sourced; no canonical replacement is asserted because the node's own text does not describe an entry door directly and a positive claim would be unsourced.

variants.note: Exactly the kind of applied classical element this node's own text rules out.

door_surround.rule: 'Ornament essentially absent: no shutters, no keystones, no applied classical elements, no material changes at an outside corner' (defining_characteristics item 7); the surround, where present at all, is flat and unornamented.
door_surround.note: Direct quote of defining_characteristics item 7. Fixes a cascade bug: the previously-resolved pilasters-and-entablature surround (english-georgian/colonial-revival, via the family splice) is exactly the applied classical element this node rules out.

variants.note: 'Attached garage on the frontage' -- inherited unmodified from ranch-style via the production-builder apparatus (lineage note against ranch-style).

garage_strategy.rule: The garage remains attached on the frontage, an unexamined structural holdover from the ranch and neo-eclectic apparatus this node otherwise reforms. Under a form-based code, the same idiom relegates the garage to an alley or a deep setback and 'produces a visibly better version of the same style' (distinguished_from vs new-urbanist-traditional).

edit_provenance.note: Not marked invented: unlike the family's general framing, this node's answer is retrieved directly from its own documented practice -- the market-dominant, as-built condition -- rather than newly authored. The better, alley-relegated answer already exists in the family as new-urbanist-traditional's own garage_strategy and is cross-referenced here rather than duplicated.

as_built_depth_range_ft.note: 'Vernacular source 8 to 10 ft full width' -- the market-built figure falls well short and is recorded diagnostically, not as a target.

porch_depth.rule: A covered space may be described as a porch only at 8 ft or more of clear depth across not less than 40 percent of the facade; shallower entry roofs are hoods and must be detailed as such (soft constraint c05).
porch_depth.note: Direct quote of constraint c05 and typical_ratios.

variants.note: Overrides the cascade's inherited value (english-georgian, via colonial-revival's family).

trim_family.rule: Flat-stock, board-and-batten-derived trim, sized against the framing module (see constraint c04) -- no surviving classical-order-derived trim tradition. This is the primary and effectively only trim system genuinely present, per this node's own bound trim-craftsman pack.
trim_family.note: Direct quote of defining_characteristics item 7 and the style's own pack-binding note for trim-craftsman.
